headline: Add compliance review workflow and endpoints for held payments
summary: Adds a compliance review service, controller endpoints, and domain events to list, release, or reject held payments. Also injects customer notification support and a hold threshold into payment processing, alongside updated hold and reject transitions on the payment entity.
business: Compliance officers gain dedicated endpoints to inspect held payments and release or reject others' payments with a mandatory rejection reason. Customers are notified during payment workflows, and payments reaching the hold threshold require compliance review before completion.

reasons.text: Compliance review endpoints require Customer authorization policy
reasons.claim: PaymentsController has [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on the class level. In ASP.NET Core, action-level [Authorize] attributes are evaluated alongside class-level attributes, meaning compliance officers without the Customer role will receive HTTP 403 Forbidden on held, release, and reject endpoints.
reasons.suggested_fix: Move the compliance endpoints to a separate dedicated controller (e.g., PaymentReviewController) protected with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Compliance)], or remove the class-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] attribute from PaymentsController and apply it per-action.
reasons.say: Compliance staff without customer permissions will be blocked with 403 errors on held, release, and reject endpoints. Ask the author to fix the authorization policy on PaymentsController.
reasons.say_facts: In ASP.NET Core, action-level [Authorize] attributes are evaluated alongside class-level attributes, meaning compliance officers without the Customer role will receive HTTP 403 Forbidden on held, release, and reject endpoints. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: ReleaseAsync transfers funds from payer account instead of Suspense account
reasons.claim: In ReleaseAsync, funds are transferred from payment.FromAccountId directly to the payee and FeeIncome accounts instead of transferring from BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, currency). This bypasses the Suspense account and attempts to debit the customer account a second time.
reasons.suggested_fix: Use BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, payment.Currency) as the source account for both payee transfer and fee transfer in ReleaseAsync.
reasons.evidence:
transferId = await ledger.PostTransferAsync(
                        payment.FromAccountId,
                        payment.ToAccountId,
                        Math.Round(payment.Amount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero),
                        reference,
                        ct);
reasons.say: Releasing a held payment debits the customer account a second time instead of using the Suspense account. Ask the author to change ReleaseAsync to transfer funds from Suspense.
reasons.say_facts: This bypasses the Suspense account and attempts to debit the customer account a second time. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: RejectAsync does not return funds from Suspense account to payer
reasons.claim: RejectAsync updates the payment status to Rejected but never executes a ledger transfer. Funds held in Suspense for the rejected payment are never refunded to the payer's account.
reasons.suggested_fix: In RejectAsync, invoke ledger.PostTransferAsync transferring (amount + fee) from BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, payment.Currency) to payment.FromAccountId before saving and committing.
reasons.say: Rejecting a held payment leaves the customer's money stranded in Suspense with no refund. Ask the author to add the Suspense-to-payer refund transfer in RejectAsync.
reasons.say_facts: Funds held in Suspense for the rejected payment are never refunded to the payer's account. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Payment.Hold() is called unconditionally for all payments
reasons.claim: All payments are transitioned to Held and saved to the database prior to evaluating if the payment should actually be held. If an error occurs prior to completion or if concurrent queries inspect the database, normal payments are incorrectly recorded and exposed as Held.
reasons.suggested_fix: Only call payment.Hold() when shouldHold is true. For normal payments, leave status as Pending until payment.Complete(transferId) is called.
reasons.say: Every payment is temporarily saved as held even when no review is needed, risking wrong statuses for customers if something fails. Ask the author to evaluate hold rules before calling Payment.Hold().
reasons.say_facts: If an error occurs prior to completion or if concurrent queries inspect the database, normal payments are incorrectly recorded and exposed as Held. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Held payments do not transfer funds to the Suspense account
reasons.claim: When a payment qualifies for review (shouldHold is true), the code skips the standard transfer block but never posts a transfer to move (amount + fee) from the payer to the Suspense account. Payer funds remain in their account unreserved while the payment is held.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add an else branch when shouldHold is true that calls ledger.PostTransferAsync transferring (amount + fee.Amount) from request.FromAccountId to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, fromAccount.Currency).
reasons.say: When a payment is held, money stays in the customer's account instead of moving to Suspense, so it could still be spent. Ask the author to transfer amount plus fee to Suspense upon hold.
reasons.say_facts: Payer funds remain in their account unreserved while the payment is held. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Releasing a held payment transfers from payer account instead of Suspense
reasons.claim: ReleaseAsync transfers payment.Amount and payment.Fee from payment.FromAccountId rather than the Suspense account. If funds had been held in Suspense, this would double-debit the customer and leave Suspense funds stranded.
reasons.suggested_fix: Use BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, payment.Currency) as the source account for both the payee transfer and the fee income transfer.
reasons.evidence:
transferId = await ledger.PostTransferAsync(
                        payment.FromAccountId,
                        payment.ToAccountId,
                        Math.Round(payment.Amount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero),
                        reference,
                        ct);
reasons.say: Releasing a held payment tries to debit the customer again while leaving money stuck in Suspense. Ask the author to update ReleaseAsync so it pays out from the Suspense account.
reasons.say_facts: If funds had been held in Suspense, this would double-debit the customer and leave Suspense funds stranded. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Rejecting a held payment does not refund funds from Suspense to payer
reasons.claim: RejectAsync marks the payment status as Rejected but fails to post any ledger transfer. Funds sequestered in the Suspense account are never returned to the customer's account.
reasons.suggested_fix: Call ledger.PostTransferAsync in RejectAsync to transfer (payment.Amount + payment.Fee) from BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, payment.Currency) back to payment.FromAccountId.
reasons.say: Rejecting a held payment never returns sequestered funds from Suspense back to the customer. Ask the author to post the refund transfer in RejectAsync when a payment is rejected.
reasons.say_facts: Funds sequestered in the Suspense account are never returned to the customer's account. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Held payments do not transfer funds to the Suspense account
reasons.claim: When a payment qualifies for compliance hold, PaymentService marks it as Held but completely skips calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync. The customer's funds remain in their account instead of being sequestered in Suspense, allowing the customer to withdraw or spend the money during review.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add an else branch when shouldHold is true to invoke ledger.PostTransferAsync transferring (amount + fee) from request.FromAccountId to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, fromAccount.Currency).
reasons.say: Held payments skip reserving funds in Suspense, letting customers withdraw or spend money during compliance review. Ask the author to post the transfer to Suspense when a payment is held in PaymentService.
reasons.say_facts: The customer's funds remain in their account instead of being sequestered in Suspense, allowing the customer to withdraw or spend the money during review. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: High business impact
reasons.detail: Compliance officers gain dedicated endpoints to inspect held payments and release or reject others' payments with a mandatory rejection reason. Customers are notified during payment workflows, and payments reaching the hold threshold require compliance review before completion.
reasons.say: This change adds high-impact fraud controls affecting customer notifications, compliance reviews, and money flows. Verify that compliance staff workflows, rejection reasons, and the 5,000 EUR hold threshold match bank policy.
reasons.say_facts: This change has a high impact on customers or money: Compliance officers gain dedicated endpoints to inspect held payments and release or reject others' payments with a mandatory rejection reason. Customers are notified during payment workflows, and payments reaching the hold threshold require compliance review before completion. Confirm the business owner agrees.

reasons.text: Class-level Customer authorization policy blocks Compliance endpoints
reasons.claim: In ASP.NET Core, authorization attributes combine additively. Because PaymentsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level, adding [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Compliance)] on Held, Release, and Reject requires callers to satisfy both policies, rejecting compliance officers with 403 Forbidden.
reasons.suggested_fix: Move the compliance endpoints to a dedicated controller (e.g. PaymentReviewController) or apply [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] only to customer-facing actions.
reasons.evidence:
[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]
public sealed class PaymentsController : ControllerBase
reasons.say: Compliance officers will get 403 errors because the controller requires both customer and compliance permissions together. Ask the author to separate compliance endpoints or remove the class-level customer restriction on PaymentsController.
reasons.say_facts: Because PaymentsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level, adding [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Compliance)] on Held, Release, and Reject requires callers to satisfy both policies, rejecting compliance officers with 403 Forbidden. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Unbounded static ConcurrentDictionary leaks SemaphoreSlim instances
reasons.claim: PaymentLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim per Guid payment ID but never removes entries after completion or failure. In a long-running process, this dictionary grows without bound.
reasons.suggested_fix: Rely on database-level row locking or remove the semaphore key when lock count reaches zero to avoid unbounded memory growth.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> PaymentLocks = new();
reasons.say: A lock entry is created for every payment and never removed, slowly leaking memory in long-running services. Ask the author to clean up or bound the PaymentLocks cache after review completes.
reasons.say_facts: In a long-running process, this dictionary grows without bound. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: ReleaseAsync debits payer account instead of Suspense account
reasons.claim: ReleaseAsync transfers money from payment.FromAccountId directly to the payee and FeeIncome. Under the Suspense accounting model, the customer's funds were already debited upon hold, so releasing must transfer amount and fee out of the Suspense account.
reasons.suggested_fix: Use BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, payment.Currency) as the source account for ledger transfers in ReleaseAsync.
reasons.evidence:
transferId = await ledger.PostTransferAsync(
                        payment.FromAccountId,
                        payment.ToAccountId,
                        Math.Round(payment.Amount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero),
                        reference,
                        ct);
reasons.say: Releasing a payment debits the customer's account directly instead of Suspense, risking double charges or failed payouts. Ask the author to source both amount and fee from Suspense in ReleaseAsync.
reasons.say_facts: Under the Suspense accounting model, the customer's funds were already debited upon hold, so releasing must transfer amount and fee out of the Suspense account. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: RejectAsync omits required ledger refund from Suspense account
reasons.claim: RejectAsync transitions the payment status to Rejected in the database but executes no ledger transfer whatsoever. The held funds (amount + fee) are never returned to the payer's account.
reasons.suggested_fix: In RejectAsync, post a ledger transfer of (payment.Amount + payment.Fee) from BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, payment.Currency) to payment.FromAccountId before saving.
reasons.say: Rejected payments change status without returning held money from Suspense, leaving customers out of pocket. Ask the author to refund amount plus fee from Suspense to the payer in RejectAsync.
reasons.say_facts: The held funds (amount + fee) are never returned to the payer's account. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Held payments bypass Suspense account in hold workflow
reasons.claim: When shouldHold is true, PaymentService marks the payment as Held but completely skips posting any ledger transfer. The requirement specifies that (amount + fee) must be transferred from the payer's account to the bank's Suspense account upon hold.
reasons.suggested_fix: When shouldHold is true, call ILedger.PostTransferAsync to transfer amount + fee from request.FromAccountId to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, fromAccount.Currency).
reasons.say: Held payments do not move money into Suspense, breaking the bank's fraud-hold protection. Ask the author to transfer amount plus fee from the payer to Suspense whenever a payment is held.
reasons.say_facts: The requirement specifies that (amount + fee) must be transferred from the payer's account to the bank's Suspense account upon hold. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Manual JSON stream reading bypasses ASP.NET Core model binding
reasons.claim: The controller introduces ReadOptionalJsonBodyAsync to manually read Request.Body with a StreamReader and deserialize RejectPaymentRequest. This reinvents standard MVC model binding, introduces unnecessary custom plumbing, and increases controller maintenance overhead.
reasons.suggested_fix: Replace ReadOptionalJsonBodyAsync with standard ASP.NET Core model binding using [FromBody] RejectPaymentRequest? request in the Reject action signature.
reasons.say: Reading the request body manually bypasses standard validation and adds unnecessary maintenance risk for staff. Ask the author to replace ReadOptionalJsonBodyAsync with standard ASP.NET Core model binding.
reasons.say_facts: This reinvents standard MVC model binding, introduces unnecessary custom plumbing, and increases controller maintenance overhead. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Unconditional call to payment.Hold() misrepresents domain lifecycle
reasons.claim: Every new payment is transitioned to Held status and saved to the database regardless of whether it meets hold criteria. Only after saving is shouldHold checked to conditionally complete the payment, which distorts the domain lifecycle and introduces redundant database round-trips for normal payments.
reasons.suggested_fix: Only call payment.Hold() when shouldHold evaluates to true; otherwise, keep the payment in its initial state and complete it directly.
reasons.say: Normal payments are briefly stored as held before checking the rules, distorting payment history and adding database load. Ask the author to only transition status to held after confirming hold criteria apply.
reasons.say_facts: Only after saving is shouldHold checked to conditionally complete the payment, which distorts the domain lifecycle and introduces redundant database round-trips for normal payments. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Unbounded memory growth from static SemaphoreSlim dictionary
reasons.claim: PaymentLocks retains a SemaphoreSlim for every payment ID passed to ReleaseAsync or RejectAsync without any eviction or removal mechanism. In long-running processes, this causes continuous memory accumulation.
reasons.suggested_fix: Use a bounded cache, clean up keys after releasing the lock if no waiters remain, or rely on database-level row locking/optimistic concurrency rather than an unbounded static dictionary.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> PaymentLocks = new();
reasons.say: Storing a permanent lock object per reviewed payment will steadily consume server memory over time. Ask the author to remove entries after use or use a bounded locking mechanism in PaymentLocks.
reasons.say_facts: In long-running processes, this causes continuous memory accumulation. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Class-level Customer authorization policy blocks Compliance endpoints
reasons.claim: In ASP.NET Core, Authorize attributes at the class and action level combine additively. Because PaymentsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], compliance officers accessing Held, Release, or Reject must satisfy both Customer and Compliance policies, resulting in HTTP 403 Forbidden for officers without Customer role permissions.
reasons.suggested_fix: Move the compliance endpoints to a separate controller (e.g. PaymentReviewController) protected only with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Compliance)], or apply Customer policy to specific customer action methods rather than the entire controller class.
reasons.evidence:
[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]
public sealed class PaymentsController : ControllerBase
reasons.say: Compliance staff cannot access review endpoints unless they also hold a customer role, blocking fraud operations. Ask the author to ensure Held, Release, and Reject on PaymentsController do not require the Customer policy.
reasons.say_facts: Because PaymentsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], compliance officers accessing Held, Release, or Reject must satisfy both Customer and Compliance policies, resulting in HTTP 403 Forbidden for officers without Customer role permissions. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Static PaymentLocks dictionary grows without bound
reasons.claim: PaymentReviewService creates and stores a SemaphoreSlim in a static ConcurrentDictionary for every reviewed paymentId without ever removing entries, introducing unbounded memory growth over the lifetime of the application.
reasons.suggested_fix: Clean up locks when no longer contested or use a bounded cache/evicting lock store.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> PaymentLocks = new();
reasons.say: Retaining a lock entry forever for every reviewed payment causes unbounded memory growth in PaymentReviewService. Ask the author to clean up or bound PaymentLocks so production stability is not affected.
reasons.say_facts: PaymentReviewService creates and stores a SemaphoreSlim in a static ConcurrentDictionary for every reviewed paymentId without ever removing entries, introducing unbounded memory growth over the lifetime of the application. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: No test coverage for payment hold evaluation or Suspense transfer in PaymentService
reasons.claim: The test suite in FraudHoldTests tests only IPaymentReviewService guard paths and contains no unit or integration tests for PaymentService.PayAsync. Consequently, critical requirements—holding payments >= 5,000 EUR to new payees, routing funds to Suspense, and allowing smaller or repeat payments through—are completely unverified.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add unit tests for PaymentService.PayAsync asserting that payments >= 5,000 EUR to new payees transition to Held, post transfers to the Suspense account, publish PaymentHeld, and leave regular or repeat payments in Completed.
reasons.say: There are no tests checking whether large payments to new payees are actually held or routed to Suspense. Ask the author to add PaymentService.PayAsync tests covering hold thresholds, repeat payees, and Suspense transfers.
reasons.say_facts: Consequently, critical requirements—holding payments >= 5,000 EUR to new payees, routing funds to Suspense, and allowing smaller or repeat payments through—are completely unverified. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Missing tests for successful execution of ReleaseAsync and RejectAsync
reasons.claim: FraudHoldTests only checks exception handling for missing payments, wrong roles, and blank rejection reasons. There are zero tests asserting that ReleaseAsync and RejectAsync successfully complete transfers from Suspense, update payment status to Completed/Rejected, and publish domain events.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add tests for successful ReleaseAsync and RejectAsync flows asserting that ledger transfers source funds from Suspense, payment statuses update appropriately, and domain events/notifications are dispatched.
reasons.say: Happy paths for releasing and rejecting held payments are untested, leaving fund transfers and notifications unverified. Ask the author to add tests in FraudHoldTests confirming Suspense payouts, refunds, statuses, and events.
reasons.say_facts: There are zero tests asserting that ReleaseAsync and RejectAsync successfully complete transfers from Suspense, update payment status to Completed/Rejected, and publish domain events. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Missing negative tests for self-decision and non-Held status checks
reasons.claim: The requirement mandates that an officer attempting to release or reject their own payment throws UnauthorizedAccessException, and attempting to release or reject non-Held payments throws InvalidOperationException. FraudHoldTests omits tests for these validation branches.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add test cases covering self-release/self-rejection by matching customer ID with current user ID, as well as attempting release/rejection on Pending, Completed, or Rejected payments.
reasons.say: Self-approval blocks and invalid-status checks lack tests, risking compliance officers releasing their own payments or non-held payments. Ask the author to add negative tests for these rules in FraudHoldTests.
reasons.say_facts: FraudHoldTests omits tests for these validation branches. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: 13 changed method(s) have no usable test evidence
reasons.say: Thirteen changed methods, including PaymentsController endpoints, lack usable test evidence, leaving edge cases unverified before release. Check which controller and service paths still need automated tests before signing off.
reasons.say_facts: 13 changed parts of the code are not covered by any working test. Read them yourself or ask for tests.

reasons.text: Reviewer asks a human to check What
reasons.detail: Requirement match is partial: While domain events, review service interfaces, and HTTP endpoints were added, the core suspense accounting mechanism is missing: funds are never transferred to Suspense when payments are held, ReleaseAsync transfers from the payer rather than Suspense, RejectAsync does not refund funds from Suspense to the payer, and payments are unconditionally marked as Held before
reasons.say: Core Suspense accounting and hold sequencing are broken, putting customer balances and fraud stops at risk. Ask the author to fix Suspense transfers on hold, release, and reject, and only hold qualifying payments.
reasons.say_facts: The reviewer is not sure the change does everything the requirement asks. Compare the change with the requirement.

reasons.text: Reviewer asks a human to check Where
reasons.detail: Tier HIGH → full human read and 2 sign-off(s) required
reasons.say: Because this change touches high-risk payment flows and compliance controls, a full code read and two sign-offs are required. Check that all critical accounting and authorization fixes are completed before approving.
reasons.say_facts: The change touches a sensitive part of the bank. Check that only the intended places changed.

reasons.say: Not checked (switched off by the team's coverage level, or did not run): Requirement. Not counted as passed; trust cannot be High.
